_why: SelectProcessor::process's batch-eligible stream-stream JOIN arm applies WHERE via apply_where_to_joined_batch and then returns the packed batch DIRECTLY — the SELECT list is never applied. Measured: `SELECT a.auction_id, a.category, r.tier FROM auction a JOIN person r ON a.seller = r.person_id WHERE a.category = 10` emits [a.seller, r.person_id, a.auction_id, r.tier, a.category] — five columns for a three-column SELECT. It is the projection sibling of #1413/#1414, where these SAME fast paths silently dropped WHERE: the pattern is a fast path that returns the packed batch and skips a clause the query asked for. Pre-existing; it became visible only when #1988 collapsed the dual bare/qualified spelling that was masking it. The Stage-1 analysis (merged #2020) went through FOUR revisions; its final recommendation is Mechanism C (Arrow RecordBatch::project) with three hard requirements, each discovered by a separate blocked review round.

anchors._note: the #1413/#1414 WHERE fix. The SELECT projection is its missing sibling — the arm calls this and then returns.
name->index against the packed batch. EXACT-MATCH (schema().index_of) — insufficient alone, see acceptance

the #594 Case 6 TEMPLATE for the SystemCol append (:132-141). NOT callable from the join arm — it takes a plan::Schema and is gated by is_safe_project_over_limit requiring Project{Limit{Scan}}. Copy the append shape, do not call it.

blast_radius._note: 15 refs / 3 files. THREE call sites in select.rs (:979, :1086, :1200) but only ONE is in scope — see acceptance.

grammar_reference._note: The reproduction is a real JOIN + WHERE query. Clause order post-#1962: SELECT -> FROM -> JOIN -> WHERE -> WINDOW -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> ORDER BY -> LIMIT. DO NOT GUESS SQL SYNTAX.

tests._note: fail_to_pass name indicative. REQUIRED: a test proving a 3-column SELECT over a batch-eligible stream-stream JOIN emits 3 data columns, verified to FAIL against master (which emits 5). batch_join_where_test.rs PINS THE CURRENT WRONG BEHAVIOUR BY DESIGN — its comment says the projection is dropped and why asserting the bare name would re-hide it. It MUST be updated, not preserved; that is the one existing test this change legitimately rewrites.

acceptance: the batch-eligible stream-stream JOIN arm at select.rs:1086 applies the SELECT list before returning

ONLY that arm is changed. select.rs:979 is UNREACHABLE (its gate is_eligible_equi_conditions rejects NonEqui, and builder.rs:478 constructs only NonEqui) — do not 'fix' it. The third site :1200 must be INVESTIGATED and reported: if it also drops the projection it is the real stream-TABLE instance, and that is a finding, not necessarily this PR's fix

a plan-time ELIGIBILITY gate: RecordBatch::project can neither rename a column nor evaluate an expression, and this path has NO SELECT-shape fall-through, so AliasedColumn / Expression select-lists must either be handled or make the batch arm ineligible at plan time
a QUALIFIED-AWARE resolver: resolve_col_indices is exact-match and the packed batch carries canonical qualified names, so an unqualified SELECT over a join hard-errors today
the system-column indices are appended explicitly (n_data + 0..SystemCol::COUNT) — StreamRecord::from_batch PANICS on a missing required system column
batch_join_where_test.rs updated to assert the projected shape, with its rationale comment rewritten
forbidden: do not change select.rs:979 — it is dead code from the SQL parser pipeline; fixing it would make an unreachable arm look exercised
do not call compute_limit_project_indices — it takes a plan::Schema and is gated on a Project{Limit{Scan}} shape the join arm does not have. Copy its SystemCol append, do not reuse the function
do not implement Mechanism A (the interval_join.rs per-row rebuild template) — rejected in the analysis as the only option that hand-rolls per-row metadata
do not implement Mechanism B (decoupling apply_post_join_select) — larger and separate; its architectural argument stands as its own issue
do not create a branch: the worktree is already on the branch velo-dispatch cut for you
